claim: Try the four-bar sample without saving it to your real songs.
where: landing action, demo banner, README, Privacy
sandbox: fresh browser context; create a real local song, enter /demo, edit and reset the sample; assert only demo:gridsong.song.v1 changes

claim: Songs save on this device.
where: landing facts, composer save state, README, Privacy
sandbox: fresh /demo context; toggle a note, reload, and assert the demo song restores while the real key stays absent

claim: Exports WAV and MIDI in your browser.
where: landing facts, export controls, README, Privacy, Terms
sandbox: fresh /demo context with the shipped sample; assert both downloadable file types

claim: Copied song links contain the whole song.
sandbox: fresh /demo context; copy the shipped sample link, open it in a new page, and assert its title, settings, and active notes restore

claim: Works offline after the first visit.
sandbox: dedicated browser context; visit /demo, wait for its service worker, go offline, reload, and assert the demo grid remains usable

claim: No account, ads, or tracking are required to compose in the demo.
sandbox: fresh /demo context; record every request during composition and demo-gallery opening, assert same-origin only and no account fields

claim: The delivered app sets no cookies and loads no third-party fonts or scripts.
sandbox: fresh /demo context; collect response headers and resource URLs, then assert no Set-Cookie, no browser cookies, and same-origin resources only

claim: Gridsong has no account-based backup; local composition changes stay in browser storage until copied or exported.
sandbox: fresh browser context; compose a local song, record requests, and assert its only persisted copy is the local song key with no gallery or account request

claim: Students can make a song by turning notes on and off in the grid.
sandbox: fresh /demo context; toggle a grid note and assert its pressed state and saved composition change

claim: Choose major, minor, pentatonic, or chromatic scales across one to four octaves, in one to 64 bars at 50–200 BPM.
sandbox: fresh /demo context; select every documented boundary and assert the controls, visible one-bar grid, and tempo output update

claim: Choose four melody sounds, plus kick and clap.
sandbox: fresh /demo context; assert the four labelled melody controls and turn on each dedicated percussion row

claim: Use the grid by keyboard.
sandbox: fresh /demo context; use Space to toggle a note and ArrowRight to move focus

claim: Audio starts only after a user presses Play.
sandbox: fresh /demo context with an AudioContext construction observer; assert no context before Play and one after the user click

claim: Development and the deployed gallery Function use Node 22, and the production static output is dist/.
sandbox: deployment-contract test asserts the Node 22 engine/runtime and production output location

claim: Students can send a nickname and song directly to the teacher’s projector board.
sandbox: two fresh browser contexts and a same-origin gallery service fixture; assert pass → direct submit → teacher poll with no ticket pasting

claim: A student class pass works on another device to submit a song, but cannot read the teacher’s board.
sandbox: API capability test proves a student key cannot satisfy the teacher-key read guard while the teacher key can

claim: The teacher access key is stored in the teacher’s browser and is not included in a student class pass.
sandbox: fresh browser context and gallery fixture; create a board, inspect the local access record, and decode the copied pass to assert it has no teacher key

claim: Only the class pass, nickname, and song are sent with a gallery submission.
sandbox: fresh browser context and same-origin gallery fixture; intercept the client submission and assert its JSON keys are exactly submitKey, nickname, and song

claim: The gallery stores a nickname, composition, submission time, expiry, and hashed access keys; it does not store raw access keys.
sandbox: API storage-shape test asserts the persisted gallery and submission records contain the documented fields and hashes rather than raw capabilities

claim: Class boards close after 90 days.
sandbox: API policy test asserts the exact 90-day retention duration used to create class boards

claim: Expired gallery records are rejected and removed in bounded cleanup during later board creation.
sandbox: API policy test exercises an expired board response and a 501-row cleanup fixture, asserting a 410 response and a 500-record cleanup cap

claim: Teachers can remove a gallery submission before the board expires.
sandbox: fresh browser context and gallery fixture; create a board containing a submission, confirm removal, and assert the teacher-key DELETE request

claim: A class board accepts up to 120 songs and tells clients when to retry.
sandbox: API response test asserts the full-board 429 has a numeric Retry-After header; live capacity smoke repeats it against deployment

claim: The composer fits a 390px phone screen.
sandbox: 390×844 browser project; assert no page-level horizontal overflow

claim: Mistyped addresses show a not-found page with a way back.
sandbox: fresh desktop and 390×844 browser contexts; request /no-such-page, assert HTTP 404, accessible page content, no overflow, and successful recovery to the composer

claim: Every marked README, Privacy, and Terms product claim has a matching inventory entry and tagged regression test.
sandbox: repository contract test scans documentation claim markers and asserts each ID is declared with a test whose source contains the exact @claim tag
